prev_agent: Done. The structural change: **HTML** — there's now a single `<div class="title-bar" data-kind-primary>` at the top of `#app`, holding the trigger. The per-pane `.titlebar-drag` divs in sidebar/content are now empty 46px spacers. **CSS**: - `.titlebar-drag` lost its `-webkit-app-region: drag`. It's just a height spacer now so the nav/content start below the title-bar overlay. - `.title-bar` is `position: fixed` across the top, `-webkit-app-region: drag` (so the user can still drag the window from the title bar), `pointer-events: none` so it doesn't block clicks on whatever's below, `z-index: 10`. - `.sidebar-trigger` is `position: absolute` (relative to the fixed title-bar), `pointer-events: auto`, `-webkit-app-region: no-drag`. Same `top: 10px` / `left: 80px` (darwin) coordinates. Why this works in both states: the title-bar drag region is always present at the button's pixels regardless of sidebar collapse state, and the button is its descendant — so the `no-drag` correctly cuts the hole. Previously, when collapsed, the button was descendant of the now-zero-area sidebar drag region, while the actual drag region under the cursor came from `.content .titlebar-drag` (a different DOM tree), so no hole was cut and the OS captured clicks as window-drag.
